**UNO – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | |---------|---------------| | **Deck** | Standard UNO set (108 cards):
• 90 numbered cards (0–9) in four colors (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow).
• 8 “Skip”, 8 “Reverse” and 8 “Draw Two” cards.
• 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score at least **1,000 points** over one or more rounds. Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes out. | --- ### 1️⃣ Setup 1. Shuffle the whole deck face down → create the *draw pile*. 2. Deal each player **7 cards**, dealt clockwise. 3. Flip the top card of the draw pile onto the discard pile; this starts play. - If it’s an action card (`+2`, `Skip`, etc.), treat it as if it had just been played (see §5). - A Wild/Draw‑Four cannot start a round unless no other playable card exists—if so, reshuffle into new draw pile until a non‑wild appears. 4. Place remaining cards face down as the *draw pile*. The next card on top becomes the *discard pile*'s starting point. --- ### 2️⃣ Turn Order & Play Direction - Players sit around a table; turn order moves **clockwise** initially. - When a **“Reverse”** card is played: - In games with ≥ 3 players, direction simply flips (now counter‑clockwise). - With exactly two players, a Reverse acts like a Skip (the opponent loses their turn). --- ### 3️⃣ Playing Cards On your turn: 1. Look at the top card of the discard pile. 2. You may lay down **one** card that matches either: - Its color, OR - Its value/symbol, OR - It’s a Wild/Wild Draw Four. 3. After playing, immediately place the card on the discard pile and resolve its effect (§5). If you have **no legal move**: - Draw **one** card from the draw pile. - If that drawn card can legally be played, you may do so right away (you’re not required to keep it). - Otherwise, end your turn without playing anything. --- ### 4️⃣ Going Out (“UNO!”) When you drop your last card: 1. Say **“UNO!”** before anyone else has seen your hand. 2. Failure to shout "UNO!" results in a penalty: draw **two** extra cards after your normal turn ends. After shouting correctly, you still follow through with any pending effects of the last card (e.g., drawing cards due to +2). --- ### 5️⃣ Action Card Effects | Card | Effect | How it works | |------|--------|--------------| | **Skip** | Next player misses their entire turn. | Immediately skip them. | | **Reverse** | Change play direction. | See §2. | | **Draw Two (+2)** | Opponent draws two cards and forfeits their turn. | They add those cards to their hand and lose the chance to play. | | **Wild** | Player chooses any color to continue play. | Pick a color; the next player must match that color or another wild. | | **Wild Draw Four** | Same as Wild but also forces the next player to draw four cards and miss their turn. | Only allowed if you truly have no matching colored card. If challenged successfully, you give back the four cards instead. | #### Challenging a Wild Draw Four - If you suspect the previous player lied (i.e., they actually had a matching color), challenge immediately after the card was laid. - Both players reveal their hands. • If the challenger **does** have a matching color, the challenger pays the penalty (draw 4). • If the challenger does **not** have such a card, the original player must pay the penalty (draw 4). The challenging player then continues normally. --- ### 6️⃣ Scoring Once a player discards all his/her cards: 1. Add up the values of the cards left in each opponent's hand: - Numbered cards: face value (0–9) - Skip / Reverse / Draw Two: **20** - Wild / Wild Draw Four: **50** 2. Winner receives that total as points. 3. Start a new round with fresh shuffling and dealing. First player to reach **≥ 1,000 points** wins the overall game. *(Optional variations)* - Some groups use different target scores (500, 2000). - Others allow “Stacking”: multiple +2/+4 cards can stack on each other, forcing cumulative draws. --- ### 7️⃣ Common House Rules | Rule | Description | |------|-------------| | **No “Play All”** | Even if you could finish with several cards, only one card per turn is permitted. | | **Card Replacement** | If you run out of space while holding many cards, you may swap a held card with one from the discard pile under certain house agreements. | | **Silent UNO** | Some players prefer silent “uno”; others insist on vocal confirmation. Clarify beforehand! | Enjoy the fast pace, colorful strategy, and occasional chaos that makes UNO a classic party favorite!
